what_its_for: Doxycycline is an antibiotic used to treat many types of bacterial infections, including chest infections, skin infections, urinary tract infections, sexually transmitted infections like chlamydia, Lyme disease, and certain eye infections. It is also used to treat acne and to prevent malaria when traveling to certain areas.
how_to_take: Take doxycycline exactly as your doctor prescribed. Swallow tablets or capsules whole with a full glass of water (at least 8 ounces). Stay upright — sitting or standing — for at least 30 minutes after taking it to prevent irritation of your esophagus (swallowing tube). You may take it with food or milk if it upsets your stomach, unless your doctor tells you otherwise. Do not crush, break, or chew delayed-release tablets or capsules.
dosing: Your dose depends on what condition is being treated and your age or weight. A common adult dose is 100 mg twice daily or 200 mg once daily. For malaria prevention, it is usually taken once daily. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions. Finish the entire course of antibiotics even if you feel better, unless your doctor tells you to stop.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store doxycycline at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medications out of reach of children. Do not use expired doxycycline — throw it away safely. Liquid forms (suspension) should be stored in the refrigerator and discarded after the expiration date on the label.
what_to_avoid: Avoid lying down for at least 30 minutes after taking your dose. Do not take doxycycline with antacids, calcium supplements, iron supplements, laxatives containing magnesium, or bismuth subsalicylate (like Pepto-Bismol) because these products can make doxycycline less effective — space them at least 2 to 3 hours apart. Avoid prolonged sun exposure and tanning beds because doxycycline makes your skin much more sensitive to sunlight and can cause severe sunburn. Wear sunscreen and protective clothing when outdoors. Avoid taking doxycycline with dairy products alone on an empty stomach if possible, though taking it with a full meal is acceptable. Do not drink alcohol excessively while taking this medication.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor or seek emergency care if you experience: severe stomach pain, persistent nausea or vomiting, difficulty swallowing or chest pain after taking the medication, severe skin rash, hives, or blistering, swelling of your face, lips, or throat, severe headache with blurred vision or vision changes, signs of liver problems such as yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice) or dark-colored urine, watery or bloody diarrhea (even weeks after finishing treatment, as this may be a serious intestinal infection), signs of high pressure in the skull such as severe headaches or ringing in the ears, or any new or worsening symptoms.
when_it_works: You may start to feel better within a few days of starting doxycycline. However, it is very important to finish the entire prescribed course even if you feel better, to make sure the infection is fully treated and to prevent antibiotic resistance. For acne, improvement may take several weeks to a few months. For malaria prevention, start taking it 1 to 2 days before travel and continue for 4 weeks after returning.
special_populations: Children: Doxycycline is generally not recommended for children under 8 years of age because it can permanently stain developing teeth and affect bone growth. It may be used in younger children only when no safer antibiotic is available, such as for life-threatening infections. Pregnancy and Breastfeeding: Doxycycline is not recommended during pregnancy, especially after the 4th month, as it can harm the developing baby's teeth and bones. It is also not recommended while breastfeeding. Talk to your doctor about safer alternatives. Older Adults: Doxycycline is generally safe for older adults, but tell your doctor about all other medications you take to avoid interactions. Kidney or Liver Problems: Use with caution. Your doctor may adjust your dose if you have severe liver disease.
